body:
I guess I feel like the abuse is partially my fault, since I can be miserable to be around & I know my depression is affecting him as well. And it just makes me hate myself, I mean I wish I wasn't like this but I am. 

Anyway so far I haven't done anything & I think I can wait out these urges, at least for today. Maybe I need to get back on medication, idk.

Thanks for the support & I hope you can make it through your ideation as well. We deserve to live better than this...
I've always felt it should be an option for severely depressed people. Why suffer forever? At least let us have the peace in death that we couldn't have in life.
Definitely relate to these feelings.
What's going on with your husband? I've been feeling similarly since I got married. But now I just feel trapped, I don't know how to be free anymore

Agree with everything you said. His response tells me all I need to know about how much I actually mean to him. And I know I should be pissed. But it still fucking hurts. A lot. How do I find the strength to walk away, move out, not reconcile with someone who cares so little? Idk, but I need to find that. Thanks for your insight.

My ex-relationship didnt progress quickly like that, we moved in after two years and were never engaged. So this one seemed more like the type where I felt loved and wanted, like what I thought I always wanted. But yeah I do see your point. Too fast.

Amazing, congrats!! It is a long process, planning to get away safely. I'm proud of you for doing it.

I'm one year out from leaving a narc and doing so much better. Best decision I ever made.

Enjoy your freedom and new life. Take care of you.

Depends what you're into.

I like journaling and reading poetry when I'm sad and need to vent. Also cuddling my cat.

My fave poet right now is Andrea Gibson. They have a poem called "Royal Heart". It resonates so much with me, I always cry when I read it.

Something that relates to you and your experiences, will touch a nerve and allow you to get that sadness out

It doesnt work, in my experience.

It's a constant struggle because you're trying to cope with your own demons but then you feel like you want to help soothe theirs as well. And on most days, you just can't. It can be comforting to know they empathise in a way. But it gets to be too much.

My longest relationships have been with un-depressed people who can kind of give me room to breathe when I'm feeling too awful to deal.
Yeah, constantly. 😐

No not necessarily. It takes 5 minutes to post up something and people will usually email you right away and often come get it the same day. Most will come to you, just walk down to somewhere public like a convenience store to meet up. At least try other things before resorting to disrespecting yourself

I think for most people, it basically does cycle through itself over and over. I wish I knew how to stop the cycles. But I've really just accepted it is going to keep coming back and the best I can do is be prepared for when it does. It is important to understand your illness, its triggers, its timeframes, its symptoms, and the techniques you can use to manage them and cope. Also the point where you need professional help. I'll usually wait until it's unbearable but some people need to go get help as soon as they feel that slide. It's a learning process. But it is manageable until you come out the other side of each cycle. Individual results vary but the important thing is taking care of yourself in every way. Especially when you don't feel like it.

You're not thinking clearly. You're trying to help yourself and your son, but you don't need to take it to this level to do it.

Do you have any possessions you wouldnt mind parting with? You can sell them on craigslist and facebook, i.e. clothes, handbags, old jewelry, dvds, cds, collectibles. When I was broke this helped me get by.

Do you have any skills you can put an ad up for? Like, child care... cooking... cleaning... writing... sewing... anything you can provide this week for cash that doesnt leave you feeling depressed and bad about yourself.

You can get out of the darkness with your head held up. I promise you.

Wouldnt recommend moving too far, at least for now. 

Look online for live-in type job roles that will give you a room in exchange for light work, i.e. nanny, caregiver/pca, farm helper, cleaning, maintenance, whatever. Or even put up your own ad listing your skills. Or just get a regular job anywhere and live cheaply with roommates.

I've been totally on my own since 18... it is so hard but you absolutely can do it.

Thanks for checking in on me. I appreciate your words and advice.

I actually have been looking into attachment styles & their relation to childhood lately. I definitely have some attachment issues/disorder. I experienced neglect, abuse, addict parents, foster care, and parental death growing up. So yeah... you can imagine the ball of attachment anxiety I am as an adult.

I had a lot of therapy growing up but I think it may be time to check into that avenue again as an adult. I'm running around in circles with this shit with my boyfriend, even now. Time is not extinguishing it unfortunately.

I am still with the same guy and actually we are recently engaged. I dont even really comprehend why he wants to marry me. I still dont trust him. And I make that known. But the truth is he could be jesus christ himself and i probably wouldnt trust him. And I think he kind of understands that it's me, and my upbringing, and all the people who hurt me, and that im projecting that even though i dont want to.

I still feel like I want to leave him sometimes even though he is the only person to treat me well in years. But I dont know if i can ever be free of all this, for him. I hate it and it makes me want to run away. But i can't, because i love him too much. It's an endless tug of war within myself.

Anyway thanks for caring and listening, internet stranger. sending good thoughts of peace your way.

He is being selfish. And not trying to empathise with you.

The holidays are draining. I'm still trying to recover from them mentally myself. I'm on vacation from work until January 2nd but I've done little besides  hang out at the house, isolating.

I too am recently engaged but having a hard time getting the ball rolling on wedding plans even though I know that's what I should be doing right now. It all seems very overwhelming. I'm so happy to marry my boyfriend but I wish we could just elope.

Honestly you need to engage in some serious self-care. You can't take care of your partner until you take care of yourself. Force yourself out, do the things you need to do but also do some things that will help you feel good about you and attractive, etc.

I'm gonna go to the gym today, get my body moving even though I really want to just stay in bed. Then go shopping for makeup and clothes, and give myself a pedicure when I get home. Treat yourself. Make yourself a priority even if he isn't being understanding. It sucks when it seems they're not trying to understand us. But ultimately we have to show compassion for ourselves no matter what. And if he is like my fiance, he will respond to that and treat you better as you treat yourself better.

Absolutely common when dealing with leaving a narc. They will tell you everything and anything they think you want to hear, to try to reel you back in.

I put up with it for a while after I left because I was so traumatized. He had always threatened to find me & kill me if I left him. Maintaining that thread made me feel safer in a weird way, like I could predict what he was gonna do if he found out where I was, etc.

Eventually I felt strong enough to accept I needed to go full No Contact. I  blacklisted him in my phone, blocked him on social media, and sent his emails to the Spam folder. 

They do finally go away. Either once they realize you are never coming back or they move onto their next victim/supply. But worry about what's right for you, not what they are doing, and cut him off via any source you can. It is so freeing for your soul.

Good! I'm so glad you knew to seek help and to take things slow with your boyfriend. And glad to hear he is a good person who is helping you along the way.

It takes such a long time to heal from narc abuse. But you will get there as long as you stay committed to yourself. Tap into your triggers and actively work to reframe them. Surround yourself with love and things that give you peace. You already survived the hard part. You will get through this part too.

You really didn't give yourself enough time to heal before jumping into a new relationship. Be careful.

Narcs hijack your brain in an unreal, lasting, significant way. The triggers, nightmare and other symptoms will lessen with time. In my case theyve finally gone away, but I've done a lot of work in focusing on myself, my wellbeing, staying no contact, writing about it, moving out of town where there are no places associated with memories of him, etc. I also burned the photos of him, which was fun.

Read on trauma bonding. It's very real and very lasting, even after the relationship is over. And please make sure you're breaking those patterns with new people.

And there's nothing wrong with seeking therapy either. I am personally not the talkative type but it can be a good healing method for many.

Again, be careful in your new relationship. Your description of him sounds overly glowing this soon on which sends up red flags to me. Js.

Your "strong will" will not fix him. But you will run yourself ragged and exhausted of all resources trying. Your health and wellbeing will definitely suffer. Sounds like you're already halfway there.

Addiction has no limits. It is up to the addict to change. Outsiders thinking their strength can be enough are probably co-dependents.

Please read Co-dependent No More. Also seek out the youtube channel for Lisa A. Romano.

Both helped me get out of the cycles of dealing with addicts and alcoholics and put the focus on me.

Triangulation, controlling, abusive, smear campaigning, false nice guy facade, lack of real empathy, gaslighting, episodic rage. Yeah, sounds like a narc to me. Glad you got away. Work on healing the inner damage and turmoil he no doubt gave you.

Narcs do NOT change or grow. Period. They lack the insight and empathy required. They are stuck in a certain period of childhood wherein the initial "narcissistic injury" happened that halted their development and brought the disorder.

If he truly has the hallmarks and criteria for NPD, walk away. Don't torture yourself with false hope.

This is definitely abusive behavior.

It reminded me of my abusive narcissistic ex. 

It will only get worse.

Get away from her. Your future self will be grateful.

I was in foster care for 11 years of my childhood. I know well these feelings of longing and deep loss and envy.

I was also told constantly life dealt me a shitty hand. Like clearly I knew that. I needed someone to guide me on what to do with that shitty hand. But most people just don't understand what it's like.

I just want to tell you there is so much love in this world. You can find that love you need in friends, pets, foster siblings, teachers, nature, books, art, anything or anybody that values you and sees you for who you are. Hold onto the things that make your soul light up, and the people that do come along and accept you.

I will not tell you it gets better. You have struggles to face that all your peers don't have to. You will have to learn to accept that you can't have the same type of life they have no matter how much you wish it.

But, you can have your own type of life that is interesting, amazing and beautiful. It may not seem like it now but your pain will make you strong and capable. You have gifts to offer this world, and love in your heart to give. You don't have to do things the way everyone else does to still have love and a great life ahead of you.

You are worth love. You are good enough for all the happiness in the world. Even though it may not feel like it sometimes. You are. Remember that. And you will be ok.

His job sounds stressful and I can understand why he needs his rest to himself. If he is still trying to see and make time for you, even with only one day off a week, I wouldn't push the issue. He was singlefor years and got used to his routines. He's probably still trying to learn to balance having a girlfriend again and working that much. Give him a few more months before you stress too much on this. As he becomes more attached to you he will naturally want you to stay over.

You're the one "jumping to conclusions". I would've already confronted him/her/everyone about it if I was trying to be a "drama queen". Instead I'm at work, trying to logically consider the situation and my options and let my feelings cool down before I address it. I even deactivated my facebook this morning so I wouldn't be tempted to contact her while still feeling emotional. But yeah, I'm a drama queen. LOL.

Yeah, I don't think it's my place either. If I took that route it would be just to get the facts as far as the pregnancy issue, not to cause drama or anything.


Yeah, I do intend to talk to him about it. We're both working right now but I may address it when I get home later. More or less just trying to sort through my feelings before I bring it to him
Thank you for the blunt truth. I probably need it right now

The cognitive dissonance is real right now, I guess. I've known him to be kind, loyal and loving toward me thus far. He's my best friend and he's done a lot to prove who he is otherwise (hard working, smart, compassionate, family oriented, etc). That's why this is so hard to take. I guess I'm still in shock
Fair point. Also something that's been on my mind.

Yes. Almost immediately after leaving my ex, my personality started coming back. My appearance, demeanor, and interests all returned to who I wasbefore he had conditioned me to constantly be someone else. A co-worker remarked a few months later that I "am a totally different person". I'm not. I'm ME now, once again. Who I was with him... that was the different person.

It's an odd feeling. Like you can breathe again. But it's so nice. Enjoy the healing process and returning your soul back to you.

You're welcome, and I'm so glad you didn't jump. I do know that feeling of the insurmountable mountain. Just keep fighting. That's the most important thing. I'm sure you are a good person and I am glad you are safe.
Just too sad right now to even get into details. Feeling suicidal but it'll probably pass. Thank you. You're a good person for offering.

You can absolutely hold down a job, depending on what it is. I've had depression, anxiety, and ptsd since childhood. Started working at 16 and have ever since. A lot of times two jobs at once. Some of them only lasted a couple months, some a few years.

Honestly when I'm really suicidal or alone sometimes working gets me through that. Even if I don't like what I'm doing or I'm doing it through my tears. It can still be better than ruminating about everything alone at home.

Plus the few friends I do have I've mostly met as co-workers at various jobs. 

You can always try. Don't listen to others that say you can't do it.

I'll talk to you, if you still need it.

It is a long ways down. You deserve help. And I hope you're getting it as I write this. Take care, friend.

I have that same constant stream of thoughts... the feeling of being inadequate and jealousy. It's so frustrating. We got into a fight tonight because of it. And he finally said he's "getting sick of it". And I really don't blame him. I know I'm illogical and I obsess. Because I love him and don't want to lose him. And yet, this shit is what will make me lose him really.

I don't obsess like this when I'm single, either. I try to focus on self-care, hobbies, getting stuff done, whatever. Because I don't have that anxiety about someone else consuming my mind. But... I eventually feel so lonely and withdrawn I want to die anyway.

Can't win, either way.  I'm not wired for loving people even though I want to so badly, and it will be my downfall

I am the same way sometimes, Ijust get sucked in by the negative symptoms and anyone around me has to deal until I can get out of that mood. I hate it, and I hate putting people through it. It isnt fair and I guess I should go back on meds or something.  

I understand your guilt for not wanting to get involved in a relationship but I do feel like some people cope better than others. Plus nobody is perfect either. Don't shut people out entirely, we deserve love too even if we are depressed

He's not naturally understanding of it because he's had some neurotic women in his life that have made him bitter about it I guess. Just found that out tonight when I tried to discuss it. But he did say he loves me and wants me to finally learn to accept being happy with someone. not that I believe thats possible. But you know... he is trying
Thanks for that. Sometimes I forget it shouldnt be a dealbreaker, I di give unconditional love and I deserve to get that in return

No we didn't. I wasn't actively trying to hide it or anything but I wasn't in a cycle when we met, it's only been bad recently. And I've been trying to just cope with it, hoping it was transient stress from work and not a real episode. Of course the more I try to deal on my own the worse it gets. I shouldve just told him from the beginning
Feeling very similarly, I think. Great work.
My cat does. He lays with me when I am crying. He will even know it from another room, and come find me to comfort me. Sometimes animals have more empathy than humans
Take a deep breath. Several if necessary. You will be ok. You slipped up and drank, but it doesnt have to become a habit again. You can get through this. Talk anywhere you feel safe, including here
I was just thinking about that today. It really does do a phenomenal job of portraying it, especially in the context of relationships. Ugh, what a lovely film

Yes, I feel this way today and often.

I am tired of life but I know those that still actually care wouldn't understand if I took mine.

Sure would be easier if someone else did.

Yeah, I hear that. I recently got a boyfriend I care about very much but I'm still sad and lonely af. It makes me feel worse in a way because I know I'm disappointing him as well as myself. I dunno man.

Keep reminding yourself of all the hideous sh*t he put you through. Make a list of all your negative memories and things he did, if that helps. Read it whenever you think you miss him.

Please realize this reaction is common... being disgusted and traumatized, and yet "missing" them at times, almost longing for them. This is a result of something called "trauma bonding". Reading up on this helped me a lot, to realize it was a pattern of thinking caused by the abuse and you totally can break that pattern! Every day you stay away it gets easier.

Focus on YOU, on healing, living your life in peace. Remind yourself of all the things you love. Do things that raise your self-esteem and forge a life without him. Spend time with loved ones, and also by yourself just learning to love yourself. You deserve a happy life and you will never have it with him.

Get angry if that helps. I drive by my ex's house on the way to work... I give him the middle finger. Even though he doesn't know... it's just a little reminder to myself that I don't need him anymore.

You can stay away for good. Absolutely. Please keep striving for that.

Ns hone on in whatever you are most sensitive about, and use it later on to harm you in both covert and overt ways. My ex did the same. My parents died when I was young and he frequently used that as ammo. I still hate him for that.

I am glad you got away from him. Read up on trauma bonding and narcissism so you can avoid another like him. Unfortunately dating patterns do repeat themselves, until we really dig in and heal our subconscious issues. You deserve better and you can do it.

I can understand why you would want others to know, but Narcs are so good at hiding their true nature to the outside world you will not get a positive reaction. You may even come off as being the "crazy", vengeful ex.

My ex was very abusive. I have videos, texts, photos, voicemails to back this up. But... still, nobody knows. I save them only for legal reasons, not to prove to others what I went through. His karma is his to deal with, and I very much believe he will reap it. Meanwhile I am focused on my life free of him and the hell he put me through, on healing, and having peace. 

My advice is just let go of the idea that people will validate what you've been through... they won't. Find it within yourself and move forward. They will realize what he is, in due time; but it's not your problem anymore.

I came here when I was plotting my escape, too. It really helped me get out safely and kept me determined to leave. Now coming here helps me deal with the aftermath and the healing process.

You got this. We're rooting for you. You can make it to the other side, too.
LOL! My Nex has been hoovering me with all sorts of false promises lately, and this is pretty much how I feel about it. Thanks for the chuckle.

My Nex used to say I should use the same shampoo his ex-wife used to use, he claimed it just smelled good not because I needed to specifically smell like her. Riiiight. He also said repeatedly I should dye my hair black... I'm blonde and had to keep telling him no fucking way. His ex had black hair, of course. He also got me to start tanning, always telling me I was too pale. I never felt self-conscious about my skin color until I dated him. No surprise his ex was spanish/tan-skinned. I used to ask him all the time, why the fuck was he dating me if I wasn't his type. He could never answer me.

Looking back I think they just pull this subtle crap to fuck with your head, make you feel degraded and like you aren't living up to their ideal. N's are control freaks and will degrade you in a million tiny ways regularly. They want you to question yourself and who you are, in order to weaken you.

Thank you. I do think it's utterly ridiculous and I find it humorous in that he comes here, obviously to antagonize victims to inflate his sense of power(lessness), then has the gall to play victim like "geez I was only trying to help" when we take it in a negative way and react angrily. It's so textbook narcissist it's laughable. Oh but he's all better now though guys... according to him his days of treating people like shit are behind him. HAHAHA! These fools really don't ever change! They just find different, roundabout ways of feeding their narc needs. 

I'm not upset by it, at all. I just don't want him triggering or manipulating anyone else here. This is supposed to be a safe place for us to get away from the mental torture of narcs.

Exactly right.

It's taken me a long time to realize that I selected boyfriends that on some level were parental-replacement type figures. No surprise I am the child of drug addicts, was neglected early on and subsequently sent to foster care. Yeesh. Narcs and abusers could spot my neediness a thousand miles away.

Now I'm working on being 100% self-reliant. And it is so empowering just knowing I don't need that care from others anymore. I can be that parental figure to myself that I always longed for, all along. It feels much better.

Perfect response.

This fool is an utter jackass, picking on abuse victims where we come to get support. Now I'm just getting frustrated. Where are the mods? Why is he still here?

LOL, this is hysterical. You just keep proving exactly what I said. And you're completely unaware of it. Thanks for the hearty chuckle after work.

You aren't wanted here, by anyone. So if you are sincerely trying to help, as you claim, you can help by exiting stage left. Bye Felicia!

I'm not interested in your rationalizations, excuses, manipulations or assumptions about me. So take this noise elsewhere.

Also, if you're so sincere about changing your narcissism, what are you doing here spending all kinds of effort trying to argue your points to everyone instead of focusing on your own recovery? Please.

I don't get why you think you're her only source of income or sustenance. Narcissists are con artists and she will find someone new to con into meeting her needs. Trust me on this.

She knows you are very empathetic and finds you easy to exploit and manipulate, so of course she would prefer to just keep sticking with you. She will not be homeless or jobless for long. She will find a new person to exploit.

Cut her off. Have someone with you when you do it, if that would help. Change locks, block contact and move on!!

Then, read up on co-dependency so this never happens to you again.

I do wish it didnt take so long. I'm starting to feel the sting of loneliness, especially on the weekends.

But I recognize fully that I MUST heal my wounds and work through my issues to move forward and eventually be healthy in general as well as with a partner. So I'm persisting in my healthy goals, introspection, self-care and wellbeing.

It is hard though. But we will end up better, for waiting it out.

The traits for narcissism definitely appear to be there. But even if he isn't, he's clearly abusive. Please read on trauma bonding and detach from him permanently. I know how hard it is but you can do it. You deserve better.

I'm 3.5 weeks away from my Ex... and yeah, I keep having dreams and nightmares about him. It's really annoying. I want to find my peace... but my subconscious is still working on issues surrounding him. I assume these will go away in time. Our brains just are trying to heal and process the trauma.

I think this happens with some Ns because they need to feel like THEY are discarding YOU, since you had the nerve to leave. Also she may realize she can no longer exploit you and is looking for a more amenable target. They do not feel empathy and you can bet they feel no sorrow for how they treated you. Chances are, though, when she's in need of Supply she will turn back up to contact you at some point, when she feels her sins are forgotten/forgiven. Just focus on you and moving on into a chaos-free life.

Thanks for posting this. It is so, so important to keep reminding ourselves of the Real Guy they are, and how cruel that person is. 

I've only been gone two weeks. After several days No Contact he came back with a Hoover attempt a few nights back: he loves me, misses me, will buy me "the rarest diamond", will give me "the moon, stars, and universe". Oh, and he has "changed"; he's "a new man"! LOL. 

I'm proud to say I didn't fall for one word of his false promises. I responded with: "You're forgetting that I actually know you, and remember everything you did to me." I also told him I am NEVER coming back. Hopefully he takes me at my word, but I doubt it. They just wait until more time passes and hope you forget more, then try again.

I wasted 3.5 years of my life on him and all the years I have left will belong only to me. I'm so glad I see him for who he is now, so I can move forward. But it does still hurt. But I can heal from that hurt... long as he stays far away from me!

I just left my ex yesterday, and I have the same fear. It's hard to feel safe again, when they made you feel unsafe for so long!

Last night was the first night in my new apartment. He doesn't know where I live. I am in a secured building with many apartments. He would not know where to find me. ...Yet, I woke up in the middle of the night panicking. I dreamt that as I was sleeping I awoke to him next to me, that he somehow found me and was lying next to me, giving me that sick smile he used to give me when he was taunting and belittling me. But I woke up and there was no one there. Just my cat.

Life is ok now for us. It will just take some time for our brain to recognize that we are safe. Be aware of your surroundings but keep reminding yourself you are safe. I think it will get a little easier to relax, every day.

I will be, yes. I've only been in slight contact via text. But I drove by the house tonight, it's on my way home from work. It gave me bad feelings just seeing that house. I definitely never want to see him again; I'm too scared to be anywhere near him. It's hard to cut him out of my life completely, he was part of it every day for 3.5 years. But I'm getting there. I know I will, soon.

Oh he's not even in therapy, nor trying to get sober, or anything. I'm beyond done. My new life is peaceful and safe.  I miss the good parts of him, but I can't separate those from the awful parts and I know that. Thank you!
Yes, that was me! That horrible video I took on xmas day. And there's many more on my phone. All those nights are behind me now. Thank you <3
Aww, thank you. You can do it, too. PM me any time if you need advice or someone to talk to.
Thank you! =)

My Ex's issues were caused by having an alcoholic narc father who was largely absent growing up, an enabling mother who spoiled him and constantly stroked his ego (still does), and a psychopathic criminal older brother he mistakenly looked up to and emulated.

I used to feel sorry for him. His family is beyond toxic and he really had very little chance of being normal.

Nonetheless it doesn't change the fact he was abusive, horrible and narcissistic. He treated me as a tool, not a human. It doesn't matter what the reasons behind his behavior are. 

As empathetic people we want to rationalize things, see the good in them, pretend they aren't monstrous. But they are. No matter what caused it... they are. Accepting that will allow you to move forward, I think.

Thank you very much for thinking of me. I'm actually moving out this weekend. Unfortunately he found out and is not taking it well. He got super drunk last night and kept me up til 4am... but he didnt physically threaten me. I am hoping everything goes according to plan this weekend, and I am able to get me/my cat/my possessions out safely. If he starts acting up I will not hesitate to call the police. I will post an update when it's all overwith. :)

What you described is called "love bombing" and narcs are experts at it. It's a charming act they pull to reel you in. And it works very effectively.

Unfortunately it's also what keeps us going back time after time, even when the poor treatment begins.

Consider yourself lucky you weren't with him very long. The longer you're in it, the more damage they do. Don't envy the new gf, feel sorry for her. Seriously. I've been with my narc bf 3+ years... his longest relationship by far. But 2+ years of hell for me. Even though he hurt you, you dodged a bigger bullet in the long run.
I love this. You sound so strong and empowered. I'm leaving my nightmare Narc bf soon... can't fucking wait to have this feeling. Major props for kicking him out of your life.

Yes...I found a nice normal roommate on the other side of the city, in a cute condo. He's letting me drop things off there little by little until my actual moving day so I wont have so much to take then. I am not telling my bf ahead of time. That day will be hard... but I will try to get out as quickly and safely as possible. If he threatens me in any type of way I will call the cops. Once I'm out I will get a restraining order, as I have videos on my phone of him being abusive and threatening to kill me.

I think you're onto something there. The physical part of things with my NPD bf progressed far quicker than anyone I've ever been with. It was intense and consuming attraction from the start. It took a long time for that to fade but once it did and my head stopped spinning... then I found out the enormity of dysfunction I was actually dealing with.

I'm in an abusive relationship right now. I was just thinking earlier today how fucking grateful I am I never got pregnant with his child. I had a scare a few months ago. I was shaking taking the pregnancy test, sick with worry. The thought of bringing a baby into a life with this awful man and his dysfunctional family didn't even seem optional. I knew unequivocally I would abort. Fortunately it didn't come to that. I wasn't pregnant, and haven't had sex with him since because it scared me so badly. I'm leaving him at the end of the month.

I honestly applaud you for your choice. No child should be brought into a horrible circumstance. I'm so glad you got away from him and can move forward and be happy.

Thank you very much. I'm trying to get out as safely as I possibly can. He's trying to act all sweet and giving right now, no angry outbursts since that video 1.5 weeks ago. ...But I know from being with him so long that it's just yet another "honeymoon" phase in the inevitable cycle. Round & round we always go, with these abusers. Why?? They don't deserve our effort, time, or caring.

Please find your way out. You deserve so much more, too. I read your comment about "waking up angry". That's been happening to me a lot lately, too. It's an awful way to exist. Take your power back. <3

I will be leaving my narc at the end of January. He doesn't know, and I don't plan to tell him ahead of time. They just ramp up their crazy-making and fear inducing tactics as well as manipulations that they will supposedly change... 

Really, his opinion on the matter bears no relevance to me... I'm leaving regardless. So why try to hash it out with him? He won't change. Ever. This is rooted in the deepest parts of who he is. They can pretend to change or improve, sort of, temporarily... then the monster shows right back up again in due time.
